wire.headline: Utility Giant Reports Profit Drop and Announces Job Cuts
sentences: The company reported that revenue rose by 7% year over year to reach 4.26bn GBP for the quarter ending on 30 September.
Despite the increase in income, pre-tax profit fell by 12% to stand at 310m GBP.
Management announced a plan to cut 850 jobs, which represents about 6% of the total workforce.
The firm stated that two gas plants are scheduled to close by March 2027, with one facility located in Wales and the other in Kent.
CEO Marian Holt explained that the cost pressure faced by the business has been sharper than expected.
The regulator Ofgem has opened an investigation into the company's billing system.
The board decided to hold the dividend at 12.4p a share.
Shares in the company dropped by 4.2% during morning trading.

ND.headline: Energy firm faces backlash over job cuts and billing issues

sentences.text: The company reported that its pre-tax profit declined by 12% to 310m GBP.
The firm currently employs 4,800 staff in the UK.
It announced 850 job cuts, which represents about 6% of its workforce.
Since 2024, 1,200 staff left the company under a voluntary scheme.
The company stated that there would be no compulsory redundancies before January 2027.
Talks with unions are set to start on 4 November.
A Kestrel Securities analyst noted that the job cuts save 90m GBP a year.
Kestrel Securities cut its price target to 240p from 290p.
Shares closed at 268p, down 11p.
